name: Relative Clauses
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Relative Clauses module! This is how we describe people and things without starting a new sentence. In French, *Qui* and *Que* work for almost everything. In English, we have specific words for people (*Who*) and things (*Which*). The biggest challenge is translating *Dont* (Whose) and avoiding the word *What* as a connector.
contrastiveExplanation:
People vs. Things:
English: Who (People), Which (Things).
French: *Qui* acts as subject for both (L'homme qui..., Le chien qui...).

The 'What' Trap:
English: 'The book THAT I read' (Not 'The book WHAT I read').
French: *Ce que* vs *Que*. 'What' equals *Ce que*. You cannot use 'What' after a noun.

Possession (Whose):
English: The man WHOSE car is red.
French: L'homme DONT la voiture est rouge.

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Using French logic where 'Qui' applies to everything. People require 'Who'.

commonErrors.wrong: The boy that his mother is sick.
commonErrors.correct: The boy whose mother is sick.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Trying to translate 'Dont' by splitting it into 'That' + 'His'. Use 'Whose'.

commonErrors.wrong: The teacher who he is coming.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Doubling the subject. 'Who' IS the subject.

commonErrors.wrong: The house where I live in.
commonErrors.correct: The house I live in (or 'where I live').

items.questionText: This is the man ___ helped me.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Man' is a person, so we use 'Who'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est l'homme qui m'a aidé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the man who helped me.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui' for both people and things. English distinguishes: 'who' for people.

items.questionText: I lost the pen ___ you gave me.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Pen' is a thing, so we use 'Which'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai perdu le stylo que tu m'as donné.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I lost the pen which you gave me.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que' for objects. English uses 'which' (or 'that') for things.

items.questionText: This is the house ___ I live.
items.feedback: Correct! 'House' is a place, so we use 'Where'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est la maison où j'habite.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the house where I live.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'où' translates directly to 'where' for places.

items.questionText: Do you know the girl ___ is singing?

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Connais-tu la fille qui chante ?
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Do you know the girl who is singing?
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui' for people and things. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The car ___ is parked there is mine.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La voiture qui est garée là est à moi.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The car which is parked there is mine.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui' for the subject (even for things). English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: That is the school ___ I study.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est l'école où j'étudie.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: That is the school where I study.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'où' translates to 'where' for places.

items.questionText: I met a woman ___ speaks Chinese.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai rencontré une femme qui parle chinois.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I met a woman who speaks Chinese.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The dog ___ bit me ran away.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Dog' is an animal (thing) -> Which (or That).

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le chien qui m'a mordu s'est enfui.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The dog which bit me ran away.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for animals/things.

items.questionText: This is the book ___ I bought.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est le livre que j'ai acheté.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the book which I bought.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: The boy ___ is tall is my brother.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le garçon qui est grand est mon frère.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The boy who is tall is my brother.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: Here is the place ___ we met.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Voici l'endroit où nous nous sommes rencontrés.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Here is the place where we met.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'où' translates to 'where'.

items.questionText: I don't like movies ___ are sad.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je n'aime pas les films qui sont tristes.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I don't like movies which are sad.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: The teacher ___ teaches English is nice.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le professeur qui enseigne l'anglais est sympa.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The teacher who teaches English is nice.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The bag ___ is on the table is mine.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le sac qui est sur la table est à moi.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The bag which is on the table is mine.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: I remember the day ___ you were born.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je me souviens du jour où tu es né.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I remember the day when you were born.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où' (where) for time too. English uses 'when'.

items.questionText: People ___ live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Les gens qui vivent dans des maisons de verre...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: People who live in glass houses...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The bus ___ goes to the city is late.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le bus qui va en ville est en retard.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The bus that goes to the city is late.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'that' (or 'which') for things.

items.questionText: The girl ___ is dancing is my cousin.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La fille qui danse est ma cousine.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The girl that is dancing is my cousin.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'that' (or 'who') for people.

items.questionText: This is the cake ___ my mother made.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est le gâteau que ma mère a fait.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the cake which my mother made.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: Where is the key ___ opens this door?

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Où est la clé qui ouvre cette porte ?
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Where is the key which opens this door?
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: The boy ___ father is a doctor.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le garçon dont le père est médecin.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The boy whose father is a doctor.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose' for possession.

items.questionText: This is the man ___ car was stolen.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est l'homme dont la voiture a été volée.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the man whose car was stolen.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose'.

items.questionText: This is the book ___ I read yesterday.
items.feedback: Correct! You cannot use 'what' after a noun. Use 'that' or 'which'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est le livre que j'ai lu hier.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the book that I read yesterday.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'que' can sometimes be confused with 'what'. But 'what' cannot follow a noun.

items.questionText: The woman ___ I met was nice.
items.feedback: Correct! When the pronoun is the Object (I met her), you can omit it. (The woman I met).

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La femme que j'ai rencontrée était sympa.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The woman I met was nice.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: In French, you cannot omit the relative pronoun 'que'. In English, you can omit 'who/that' if it's the object.

items.questionText: I don't understand ___ you said.
items.feedback: Correct! 'What' means 'The thing that'. No noun before it.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je ne comprends pas ce que tu as dit.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I don't understand what you said.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce que'. English uses 'what' (meaning 'the thing that').

items.questionText: Do you know the reason ___ he left?

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Connais-tu la raison pour laquelle il est parti ?
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Do you know the reason why he left?
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'pour laquelle'. English uses 'why'.

items.questionText: The hotel ___ we stayed was dirty.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'hôtel où nous avons séjourné était sale.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The hotel where we stayed was dirty.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'where' (meaning 'in which').

items.questionText: The hotel ___ we visited was dirty.
items.feedback: Correct! We visited the hotel (Direct Object). No preposition 'in'. So we use 'Which'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'hôtel que nous avons visité était sale.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The hotel which we visited was dirty.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Here 'hotel' is the direct object (visited what?), so we use 'which', not 'where'.

items.questionText: Everything ___ he said is true.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Tout ce qu'il a dit est vrai.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Everything that he said is true.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce que'. English uses 'that' after 'everything'.

items.questionText: The person ___ you need to see is Mr. Paul.
items.feedback: Correct! Object pronoun omission. (The person [who] you need).

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La personne que tu dois voir est M. Paul.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The person you need to see is Mr. Paul.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French requires 'que'. English allows omitting the pronoun.

items.questionText: That is the girl ___ brother is famous.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est la fille dont le frère est célèbre.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: That is the girl whose brother is famous.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose'.

items.questionText: Is this ___ you want?

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Est-ce ce que tu veux ?
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Is this what you want?
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce que'. English uses 'what' when there is no antecedent noun.

items.questionText: The man ___ lives next door is loud.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'homme qui habite à côté est bruyant.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The man who lives next door is loud.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' as the subject.

items.questionText: The village ___ I was born is small.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le village où je suis né est petit.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The village where I was born is small.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French 'où' translates to 'where'.

items.questionText: The email ___ I sent you.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'email que je t'ai envoyé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The email that I sent you.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que'. English uses 'that' or 'which'. Never 'what' after a noun.

items.questionText: The friends ___ we invited didn't come.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Les amis que nous avons invités ne sont pas venus.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The friends we invited didn't come.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French requires 'que'. English allows omission.

items.questionText: He is the one ___ did it.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est lui qui l'a fait.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: He is the one who did it.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who'.

items.questionText: This is ___ I am talking about.
items.feedback: Correct! No noun before. 'The thing that' = What.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est ce dont je parle.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is what I am talking about.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce dont'. English uses 'what' (meaning 'the thing that').

items.questionText: The car, ___ color is red, is fast.
items.feedback: Correct! Possession for things (Whose color = Its color) is also 'Whose'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La voiture, dont la couleur est rouge, est rapide.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The car, whose color is red, is fast.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose' even for things.

items.questionText: The day ___ we met was rainy.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le jour où nous nous sommes rencontrés était pluvieux.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The day when we met was rainy.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'when' for time.

items.questionText: The man to ___ I spoke.
items.feedback: Correct! After a preposition (to), you MUST use 'Whom' for people.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'homme à qui j'ai parlé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The man to whom I spoke.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'à qui'. English requires 'whom' after a preposition.

items.questionText: The house ___ I live.
items.feedback: Correct! Preposition + Which = Where. 'In which' is formal.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La maison dans laquelle je vis.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The house in which I live.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dans laquelle'. English uses 'in which' (or 'where').

items.questionText: He passed the exam, ___ surprised everyone.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Which' refers to the whole previous sentence.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il a réussi l'examen, ce qui a surpris tout le monde.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce qui'. English uses 'which' to refer to a whole clause.

items.questionText: The woman ___ I gave the book.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La femme à qui j'ai donné le livre.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The woman to whom I gave the book.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'à qui'. English requires 'whom' after 'to'.

items.questionText: The woman ___ I gave the book to.
items.feedback: Correct! If the preposition (to) is at the end, we can use 'Who' (or 'That', or nothing).

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La femme à qui j'ai donné le livre.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The woman who I gave the book to.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French keeps the preposition before the pronoun ('à qui'). English can move it to the end.

items.questionText: He has three sons, all of ___ are doctors.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il a trois fils, qui sont tous médecins.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: He has three sons, all of whom are doctors.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: English uses 'all of whom' for people in this structure.

items.questionText: I bought some apples, some of ___ were rotten.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai acheté des pommes, dont certaines étaient pourries.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I bought some apples, some of which were rotten.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: English uses 'some of which' for things.

items.questionText: My father, ___ is 60, is retiring.
items.feedback: Correct! Non-defining clause (with commas). You CANNOT use 'That'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Mon père, qui a 60 ans, prend sa retraite.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: My father, who is 60, is retiring.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: In non-defining clauses (with commas), you cannot use 'that'. You must use 'who'.

items.questionText: The reason for ___ he came is unknown.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La raison pour laquelle il est venu est inconnue.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The reason for which he came is unknown.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'pour laquelle'. English uses 'for which'.

items.questionText: What was the name of the man ___ car you borrowed?

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Quel était le nom de l'homme dont tu as emprunté la voiture ?
frenchComparison.englishStructure: What was the name of the man whose car you borrowed?
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose'.

items.questionText: This is the pen with ___ I write.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est le stylo avec lequel j'écris.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the pen with which I write.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'avec lequel'. English uses 'with which'.

items.questionText: I spoke to the manager, ___ was very helpful.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai parlé au directeur, qui a été très utile.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I spoke to the manager, who was very helpful.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: In non-defining clauses, you cannot use 'that'.

items.questionText: Find the error: "The man who I spoke to him is here."
items.feedback: Correct! Remove 'him'. The relative pronoun replaces the object. Say 'The man I spoke to'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'homme à qui j'ai parlé est ici.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The man who I spoke to is here.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Learners often repeat the object pronoun ('him') which is redundant because 'who' is already the object.

items.questionText: All ___ glitters is not gold.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Tout ce qui brille n'est pas or.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: All that glitters is not gold.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce qui'. English uses 'that' after 'all'.

items.questionText: The company for ___ I work.
items.feedback: Correct! Company is a thing -> For which.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'entreprise pour laquelle je travaille.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The company for which I work.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'pour laquelle'. English uses 'for which'.

items.questionText: The company ___ I work for.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'entreprise pour laquelle je travaille.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The company which I work for.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: English allows moving the preposition to the end.

items.questionText: ___ you need is love.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Tout ce dont tu as besoin, c'est l'amour.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: All you need is love.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'Tout ce dont'. English uses 'All (that)'.

items.questionText: This is the best ___ I can do.
items.feedback: Correct! After superlatives (the best), we prefer 'that'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est le mieux que je puisse faire.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the best that I can do.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: After superlatives, English prefers 'that'.

items.questionText: He failed, ___ is a pity.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Which' refers to the sentence 'He failed'.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il a échoué, ce qui est dommage.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: He failed, which is a pity.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce qui'. English uses 'which' to refer to the previous clause.

items.questionText: There is no one ___ knows the answer.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il n'y a personne qui connaisse la réponse.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: There is no one who knows the answer.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who'.

items.questionText: The woman ___ called me is my aunt.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La femme qui m'a appelé est ma tante.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The woman who called me is my aunt.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: I have a cat ___ is black.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai un chat qui est noir.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I have a cat which is black.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui' for both people and things. English uses 'which' for animals/things.

items.questionText: This is the room ___ I sleep.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est la chambre où je dors.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the room where I sleep.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'where'.

items.questionText: The students ___ study hard will pass.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Les étudiants qui étudient dur réussiront.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The students who study hard will pass.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The phone ___ is on the desk is broken.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le téléphone qui est sur le bureau est cassé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The phone which is on the desk is broken.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: That is the shop ___ I bought bread.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est le magasin où j'ai acheté du pain.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: That is the shop where I bought bread.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'where'.

items.questionText: I know a man ___ plays football.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je connais un homme qui joue au football.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I know a man who plays football.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The bird ___ flies high is an eagle.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'oiseau qui vole haut est un aigle.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The bird which flies high is an eagle.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for animals.

items.questionText: Here is the cake ___ you like.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Voici le gâteau que tu aimes.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Here is the cake which you like.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: The girl ___ is laughing is happy.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La fille qui rit est heureuse.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The girl who is laughing is happy.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: This is the city ___ I work.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est la ville où je travaille.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the city where I work.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'where'.

items.questionText: I like stories ___ are funny.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'aime les histoires qui sont drôles.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I like stories which are funny.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: The doctor ___ treated me was kind.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le médecin qui m'a soigné était gentil.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The doctor who treated me was kind.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The letter ___ arrived today is for you.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La lettre qui est arrivée aujourd'hui est pour toi.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The letter which arrived today is for you.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: Sunday is the day ___ we rest.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Dimanche est le jour où nous nous reposons.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Sunday is the day when we rest.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'when' for time.

items.questionText: Students ___ are late will be punished.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Les étudiants qui sont en retard seront punis.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Students who are late will be punished.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who' for people.

items.questionText: The taxi ___ stopped was yellow.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le taxi qui s'est arrêté était jaune.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The taxi that stopped was yellow.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English can use 'that' for things.

items.questionText: The boy ___ called is my friend.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le garçon qui a appelé est mon ami.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The boy that called is my friend.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English can use 'that' for people too.

items.questionText: The food ___ I cooked is hot.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La nourriture que j'ai cuisinée est chaude.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The food which I cooked is hot.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: Show me the path ___ leads to the river.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Montre-moi le chemin qui mène à la rivière.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Show me the path which leads to the river.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'which' for things.

items.questionText: The girl ___ mother is a nurse.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La fille dont la mère est infirmière.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The girl whose mother is a nurse.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose' for possession.

items.questionText: The dog ___ leg is broken.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le chien dont la patte est cassée.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The dog whose leg is broken.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose' even for animals.

items.questionText: The movie ___ we watched was good.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le film que nous avons regardé était bon.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The movie that we watched was good.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que'. English uses 'that' or 'which'. Never 'what' after a noun.

items.questionText: The cake ___ I ate was delicious.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le gâteau que j'ai mangé était délicieux.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The cake I ate was delicious.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French requires 'que'. English allows omission.

items.questionText: Tell me ___ you want.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Dis-moi ce que tu veux.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Tell me what you want.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce que'. English uses 'what' (meaning 'the thing that').

items.questionText: That is the reason ___ I am late.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est la raison pour laquelle je suis en retard.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: That is the reason why I am late.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'pour laquelle'. English uses 'why'.

items.questionText: The house ___ I was born.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La maison où je suis né.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The house where I was born.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'where'.

items.questionText: The house ___ I bought.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La maison que j'ai achetée.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The house which I bought.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Here 'house' is the direct object, so we use 'which', not 'where'.

items.questionText: Everything ___ glitters is not gold.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Tout ce qui brille n'est pas or.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Everything that glitters is not gold.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce qui'. English uses 'that' after 'everything'.

items.questionText: The book ___ you lent me is good.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le livre que tu m'as prêté est bon.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The book you lent me is good.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French requires 'que'. English allows omission.

items.questionText: The boy ___ bike was stolen is crying.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le garçon dont le vélo a été volé pleure.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The boy whose bike was stolen is crying.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose'.

items.questionText: I don't know ___ to do.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je ne sais pas quoi faire.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I don't know what to do.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'quoi'. English uses 'what'.

items.questionText: The woman ___ lives here is nice.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La femme qui vit ici est gentille.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The woman who lives here is nice.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who'.

items.questionText: The park ___ we played is closed.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le parc où nous avons joué est fermé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The park where we played is closed.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'where'.

items.questionText: The letter ___ I wrote.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La lettre que j'ai écrite.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The letter that I wrote.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'que'. English uses 'that' or 'which'. Never 'what' after a noun.

items.questionText: The people ___ we met were friendly.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Les gens que nous avons rencontrés étaient sympathiques.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The people we met were friendly.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French requires 'que'. English allows omission.

items.questionText: She is the one ___ helped me.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est elle qui m'a aidé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: She is the one who helped me.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who'.

items.questionText: That is ___ I mean.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est ce que je veux dire.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: That is what I mean.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce que'. English uses 'what' (meaning 'the thing that').

items.questionText: The table, ___ leg is broken, is old.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La table, dont le pied est cassé, est vieille.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The table, whose leg is broken, is old.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose' even for things.

items.questionText: The year ___ we met was 2010.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'année où nous nous sommes rencontrés était 2010.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The year when we met was 2010.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où'. English uses 'when' for time.

items.questionText: The student to ___ I spoke.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'étudiant à qui j'ai parlé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The student to whom I spoke.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'à qui'. English requires 'whom' after a preposition.

items.questionText: The room ___ I sleep.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La chambre dans laquelle je dors.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The room in which I sleep.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dans laquelle'. English uses 'in which' (or 'where').

items.questionText: He won the lottery, ___ made him rich.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Which' refers to the whole previous sentence.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il a gagné à la loterie, ce qui l'a rendu riche.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: He won the lottery, which made him rich.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce qui'. English uses 'which' to refer to a whole clause.

items.questionText: The person ___ I gave the money.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La personne à qui j'ai donné l'argent.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The person to whom I gave the money.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'à qui'. English requires 'whom' after 'to'.

items.questionText: The person ___ I gave the money to.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La personne à qui j'ai donné l'argent.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The person who I gave the money to.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French keeps the preposition before the pronoun ('à qui'). English can move it to the end.

items.questionText: I have many friends, most of ___ are students.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai beaucoup d'amis, dont la plupart sont étudiants.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I have many friends, most of whom are students.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: English uses 'most of whom' for people in this structure.

items.questionText: I have many books, most of ___ are old.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai beaucoup de livres, dont la plupart sont vieux.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I have many books, most of which are old.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: English uses 'most of which' for things.

items.questionText: My mother, ___ is a doctor, works hard.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Ma mère, qui est médecin, travaille dur.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: My mother, who is a doctor, works hard.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: In non-defining clauses (with commas), you cannot use 'that'. You must use 'who'.

items.questionText: The reason for ___ he left.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La raison pour laquelle il est parti.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The reason for which he left.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'pour laquelle'. English uses 'for which'.

items.questionText: Do you know the girl ___ brother is famous?

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Connais-tu la fille dont le frère est célèbre ?
frenchComparison.englishStructure: Do you know the girl whose brother is famous?
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'whose'.

items.questionText: The tool with ___ I fixed it.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'outil avec lequel je l'ai réparé.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The tool with which I fixed it.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'avec lequel'. English uses 'with which'.

items.questionText: I met John, ___ was very nice.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai rencontré John, qui était très gentil.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I met John, who was very nice.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: In non-defining clauses, you cannot use 'that'.

items.questionText: Find the error: "The book which I read it is good."

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le livre que j'ai lu est bon.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The book which I read is good.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: Learners often repeat the object pronoun ('it') which is redundant because 'which' is already the object.

items.questionText: All ___ you say is true.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Tout ce que tu dis est vrai.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: All that you say is true.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce que'. English uses 'that' after 'all'.

items.questionText: The project for ___ I am responsible.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le projet dont je suis responsable.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The project for which I am responsible.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'dont'. English uses 'for which'.

items.questionText: The project ___ I am responsible for.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le projet dont je suis responsable.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The project which I am responsible for.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: English allows moving the preposition to the end.

items.questionText: ___ I want is peace.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Tout ce que je veux, c'est la paix.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: All I want is peace.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'Tout ce que'. English uses 'All (that)'.

items.questionText: This is the worst ___ could happen.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: C'est le pire qui puisse arriver.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: This is the worst that could happen.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: After superlatives, English prefers 'that'.

items.questionText: He lied, ___ made me angry.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il a menti, ce qui m'a mis en colère.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: He lied, which made me angry.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'ce qui'. English uses 'which' to refer to the previous clause.

items.questionText: There is someone ___ can help.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il y a quelqu'un qui peut aider.
frenchComparison.englishStructure: There is someone who can help.
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui'. English uses 'who'.
